text:
liz: Heads up — since ~14:12 UTC eu-central1 apiserver 5xxs spiked and controller-manager pods restarted a few times. GPU attach ops timing out.
omar: Looking at grafana: ephemeral port usage shot up. Nodes hitting ~61k/65536. Suspect SNAT port exhaustion.
ingest-bot: Deploy: telemetry-exporter:v2.4 rolled to eu-central1 at 14:09 UTC by omar — status: success
rachel: `dmesg` shows `nf_conntrack: table full` on node-1. `conntrack -L | wc -l` -> 61072. Lots of short-lived outbound connections to telemetry endpoints.
devops: Can we cordon/restart kube-proxy on the worst nodes and add a temporary EIP pool? EIP per node would reduce SNAT churn.
liz: cordon + drain node-1 and node-2 now. also scaling controller-manager to 4 replicas to absorb failovers.
omar: rolling telemetry-exporter back to v2.3 in eu-central1 now (new release had no connection pooling).
deploy-bot: Rollback telemetry-exporter:v2.3 initiated at 14:18 UTC by omar — status: in_progress
ingest-bot: Rollback complete — status: success
rachel: conntrack entries declining, apiserver 5xxs down ~80% after rollback. GPU attach backlog slowly clearing. Kernel logs no new nf_conntrack errors.
devops: Short-term follow-ups: request NAT pool increase, add node EIP option, and restart kube-proxy on drained nodes. Filed INC-12456 with timeline + perf graphs: https://grafana.redwood/d/abc
liz: Long-term: telemetry team to implement connection pooling and backoff; provisioner to add soft rate limits for onboarding bursts. Also need cost/runbook analysis for EIP usage. Scheduling postmortem. :memo:
